item.title: Building owners' corporation fined over worker's death
item.description:
An owners’ corporation in North Point was fined HK$149,000 at the Eastern Magistrates’ Courts on Monday for violating safety regulations over the deadly fall of a worker who had been pruning a tree.
The man, who was working at Kingsfield Garden in July last year, fell about 1.2 metres from the top of a parapet wall at the car park.
He was sent to hospital with a head injury in a conscious state, but passed away two weeks later.
The court ruled that the incorporated owners of the residential building had violated the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance after the Labour Department launched a prosecution.
Edited by Tony Sabine

item.title: Ma says TDC to step up pivot to Central Asia
item.description:
Trade Development Council chairman Frederick Ma on Monday said the body would consider scaling up its presence in Central Asia.
He said the TDC had already set up an office in Almaty, Kazakhstan’s largest city, and was planning to increase manpower there to handle increasingly active business dealings and information enquiries.
For the next step, it would study upgrading the office or setting up more branches in other Central Asian countries.
Eight companies from Belt and Road countries had, Ma added, submitted listing applications to the SAR.
He also expressed hope that more companies in emerging markets would use Hong Kong's financial expertise to expand their businesses.
Improved Sino-US relations, Ma stressed, would also be beneficial to the city.
“For Hong Kong, our exports have been very strong. Our exports recorded over 40 percent increase in the first eight months of this year,” he said.
“As a matter of fact, Trade Development Council has revised our export forecast to 42 to 47 percent recently in light of the strong exports.
“So I think that, of course, good relationship between US and China is going to help, it’s not going to hurt, and we are continuing to [do] good business particularly in the AI and semiconductor sector.”
Edited by Tony Sabine

item.title: Transport systems all ready to go at Huanggang port
item.description:
The Transport Department on Monday said all signage and information systems at the public transport interchange of the new Huanggang port facility are ready.
Information systems would, it stressed, continue to be reviewed and improved based on passenger feedback.
In a social media post, the department said it had installed additional display screens at key locations and boarding areas that show route destinations, stops and boarding positions for buses and minibuses.
Large directional signages featuring transport mode icons, route numbers and directions have also been placed at major points within the interchange.
Public transport operators, the department pointed out, had also set up route signs and queue rails to ensure boarding would be orderly.
In the initial period of the crossing's opening, it said, service ambassadors would be stationed on the second-floor concourse to help travellers choose the most suitable way to reach urban areas.
Edited by Tony Sabine

item.title: Private sponsors 'can take Games haul to next level'
item.description:
Elite Sports Committee chairman Cheng King-leung has hailed the success of the Hong Kong, China contingent at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games and called for greater private‑sector sponsorship support from local corporations and major firms.
The team wrapped up its campaign by ending up ninth on the medals table with 11 golds, 19 silvers and 24 bronzes for Hong Kong's best-ever performance in Asian Games history.
Speaking on RTHK's Backchat programme on Monday, Cheng said Hong Kong’s showing at the Asian Games had exceeded expectations.
He said officials had initially expected the medal haul to be similar to previous Games, but had been pleasantly surprised by stronger performances in several sports, singling out for special mention tennis ace Coleman Wong, who won gold at the Games and, with that, qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
In welcoming the contingent's results, Cheng stressed that long‑term success depends on stronger commercial backing.
"The success of the Hong Kong delegation reflects years of sustained investment by the Hong Kong SAR government, but I think in the immediate future, a greater commercial sponsor from our local corporations and major firms is urgently needed," he said.
He said commercial support and sponsorship is essential to the city's sport development in the years ahead, pointing to Thailand's having secured six more gold medals than the previous Hangzhou Asian Games following "a complete corporate sponsorship" programme initiated by the government.
Cheng said Hong Kong's recent success would encourage more youngsters to consider elite sport careers if post‑sport employment pathways and sponsorship support continued to improve.
He added that the scarcity of facilities must be addressed promptly and welcomed the government's plans to invest in 26 sports development projects, including the Victoria Park revamp.
Edited by Tony Sabine

item.title: Privacy watchdog probes pinhole cameras in Sha Tin gym
item.description:
The Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data (PCPD) on Monday launched a compliance check on 24/7 Fitness, after hidden pinhole cameras were discovered inside the changing rooms at its Sha Tin gym.
PCPD said the discovery had raised concerns among members of the fitness chain about their privacy and the compliance check was to ensure that their personal data is adequately protected.
The watchdog said it had required the company to provide further information on security measures it has implemented following the incident to safeguard members' personal data.
The PCPD said it would also examine whether such measures are sufficient to prevent similar incidents from recurring.
Edited by Tony Sabine

item.title: Smooth start in phased opening of Kai Tak Hospital
item.description:
The chief executive of Kai Tak Hospital, Eric Cheung, on Monday said the facility was running smoothly on its first day of operation.
Speaking after inspecting the hospital in the morning, he said a family medicine centre was among the first of its services to open – offering another healthcare option for residents in the Kowloon Central cluster.
“There are a total of 350 quotas for today (Monday), and as far as I know, this morning about 290 something quotas have been booked, so there are still a small number of quotas left for today," Cheung said of allotments for family medicine services.
“We will be starting our service gradually.
"On October 26, we will be moving our specialist outpatient clinics of surgery and neurosurgery to this place to start service, and on November 12, we will be moving our biggest specialty to start service here – that’s the department of medicine.”
Cheung said the hospital had not received any complaints from patients, with most of them able to find their way to the hospital.
Patients praised the new hospital's smooth operations, convenient transport connections and good environment.
One man said he had a better experience at Kai Tak Hospital, compared to where he used to go for follow-ups.
“Besides being a large-scale healthcare facility, everything at the hospital is impressive in scale and organised well,” he said.
“As I walked through, apart from directional signs, there were many staff and security guards around the hospital, probably because it’s the first day of service. They came up to greet me and ask if there was anything they could help with, proactively offering assistance.”
Another patient said he did not have to wait long to see a doctor, saying the process was smooth.
Edited by Tony Sabine

item.title: Youth at heart of five-year plan, Policy Address: CE
item.description:
Chief Executive John Lee on Monday said the future of the city's young people is one of the central components of Hong Kong's first five-year plan and the Policy Address he announced last month.
Speaking in a video message at the Global Youth Powerhouse Summit 2026, Lee said the younger generation would not only benefit from the city's reforms and development, it would also be the driving force behind them.
"For you, Hong Kong is where careers are built, talent is nurtured, and global horizons are within reach," Lee said.
The chief executive highlighted the Northern Metropolis as key to the city's development, describing it as a piece of land taking up one-third of Hong Kong's area that will potentially be home to a third of the population.
Three university towns in San Tin, Hung Shui Kiu and Ta Kwu Ling are at its heart, integrating education, technology, industry and talent cultivation, he said.
Beyond the Northern Metropolis, Lee also said young people could find opportunities from a new United Nations Youth Leaders Internship Programme offering placements at UN agencies, as well as expanded mainland internship and training schemes in finance, aerospace and cutting-edge research.
Lee said the government and the business sector would also jointly launch a youth employment and internship programme offering 30,000 places over the next two years.
"For our young people, I firmly believe that your opportunities ahead outweigh the difficulties," Lee said.
He added the government would join hands with all sectors to build platforms for young people to thrive in Hong Kong, across the country and on the global stage.
Edited by Tony Sabine
